summary.headline: PNGS Reva FY26 revenue rose 70% to INR439 crore and Q4 revenue rose 139% to INR138 crore, though FY26 PAT grew only 9% to INR65 crore.
summary.overview: PNGS Reva reported its first full standalone year (FY26) as a separate entity, with revenue from operations of INR439 crore (up 70% on restated FY25) and EBITDA of INR95 crore at a 22% margin. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR138 crore (up 139% YoY), with EBITDA of INR31 crore (22% margin) and PAT of INR21 crore (16% margin). Management attributed the margin dilution versus the earlier divisional period to standalone costs such as rent, inventory and logistics, and CEO/CFO/compliance functions. Management guided to 25-30% SSG and top-line growth in FY27-28, with 15 new stores over 24 months funded from IPO proceeds. Around INR55-60 crore of FY26 revenue was surplus gold received as consideration, per management.

financial_highlights.change: +70% YoY vs restated FY25 INR258 crore

segments.name: SIS (Shop-in-Shop, within P.N. Gadgil stores)
segments.commentary: 34 SIS stores at year-end (30 at start of FY26); the 30 pre-existing SIS generated about INR313 crore in FY26, and SIS-level SSG was about 40% in FY26. Management says SIS represent roughly INR350 crore of top-line and about INR330 crore of inventory; commission is 4% of sales on a blended basis, with no commission on gold.

segments.name: EBO (company-operated exclusive outlets)
segments.commentary: 2 COCO stores currently (one added post-IPO). Management's target per EBO is about INR9 crore revenue at 0.75x stock turn, about INR1.5 crore EBITDA initially, rising to INR3-3.5 crore in 3-4 years. Capex about INR20-25 crore per EBO; rent-based, asset-light.

guidance_outlook: SSG guided at 25-30% a year for FY27 and beyond, not below 25%, assuming stable gold prices; a sharp gold rally could repeat the ~40% SSG seen in FY26.
Top-line growth guided at around 25-30% for the next two years, led mainly by the SIS base and new stores.
15 new stores over a 24-month period (one already open): 6-7 in FY27 and the remainder in FY28; split about 60% Maharashtra and 40% outside, with 2 out-of-state stores in FY27.
Inventory turn expected to hold around 1.31x as new EBOs at 0.75x are offset by SSG; EBO breakeven 8-12 months in Maharashtra and 18-24 months outside.

Brand spend of 3-4% of top-line annually, plus about INR2 crore per EBO spread over 12-18 months. Gross margin may gain as brand value is loaded into diamond pricing over time, though percentage margin may fall as gold share rises.
No equity dilution expected; growth funded by internal accruals and a sanctioned debt headroom of roughly INR150-200 crore, with borrowing expansion after 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Store economics for SIS and EBOs: revenue per store and footfalls?
qa_highlights.answer: SIS commission is about 4% of sales blended, none on gold; FY26 SSG about 40%. EBO target is about INR9 crore revenue at 0.75x turn (about 2.5-3 customers a day at INR1.2 lakh bill), about INR1.5 crore EBITDA initially, rising to INR3-3.5 crore in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from around 30-32% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone costs such as separate premises rent, inventory and logistics department, and CEO, CFO and compliance functions were not borne by the division earlier. Management says these costs now load the P&L and sustain a lower EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is 28% gross margin and 22% EBITDA margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin can rise as brand value is loaded into diamond pricing; currently no brand premium is charged, and the industry runs 30-35% or up to 40-42% gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will gold price rises affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin percentage may contract as gold share rises, but management expects rupee gross profit to be maintained or grow.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to surplus gold received in exchanges?
qa_highlights.answer: It is received as consideration and sold in the open market or B2B to avoid working capital being stuck; inventory is valued at average purchase price, so no inventory gain is booked.

qa_highlights.question: Will inventory turn fall as 6-7 new EBOs open in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 1.31x to be maintained because new EBOs at about 0.75x are offset by SIS SSG; it says a fall would be limited to between 1.25x and 1.35x.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue outlook for FY27-28 and SSG?
qa_highlights.answer: SSG 25-30% and top-line growth 25-30% a year, mainly from SIS and new stores; SSG could again be around 40% if gold prices spike as in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will growth capex be funded post-IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals (about INR64 crore FY26 earnings retained), with INR150-200 crore of unused sanctioned debt; no equity dilution expected, and borrowing expansion planned after 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Will store breakevens and inventory differ by region?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra EBOs are expected to reach 0.75x turn and about INR1.5 crore EBITDA in 8-12 months; outside Maharashtra in 18-24 months. Early-stage turn could be 0.25-0.5x in the first 4-5 months.

capex_capacity: 36 stores at call date: 2 COCO EBOs (one added post-IPO) and 34 SIS; 15 new stores planned over 24 months, one already open, 14 remaining; 6-7 in FY27 and balance in FY28.
Store mix for the 15 stores: about 60% Maharashtra and 40% outside, with 2 out-of-state stores in FY27; preference for North India Tier 1 mall locations.

EBO capex about INR20-25 crore per outlet; EBO inventory of INR12-15 crore at 0.75x turn; store sizes small/medium/large need INR9-10 crore, INR12-15 crore and INR18-20 crore of inventory respectively.
SIS expansion funded by parent P.N. Gadgil from internal accruals at 3-4 stores every two years; a standalone store costs INR90-120 crore for the parent, which is why the EBO model was chosen.
IPO raised INR380 crore; INR287 crore earmarked for store expansion and working capital, INR35 crore for marketing of the 15 new stores.

Debt: INR190 crore existing loans plus INR50 crore ICICI Bank and INR40 crore SVC Bank sanctions; about INR132-150 crore utilised, leaving roughly INR150-200 crore unused headroom. No equity dilution expected; borrowing expansion after 2030.
demand_pricing: SIS (30 pre-existing stores) generated about INR313 crore in FY26; management cited SIS top-line of roughly INR350 crore across 34 stores and SIS SSG of about 40% in FY26.
FY26 average order value INR1,20,000 vs INR85,000 in FY25 (+41%); Q4 revenue INR138 crore (+139% YoY), gross margin 28%.
Around INR55-60 crore of FY26 revenue (about INR55 crore cited) was surplus gold received as consideration in buybacks/exchanges; ex-gold B2C jewellery about INR390 crore.
Guidance: SSG 25-30% a year for FY27 and beyond, not below 25%, if gold prices stay stable; top-line growth 25-30% for the next two years.
Price architecture: entry INR15,000-35,000; everyday INR35,000-1.5 lakh; occasion INR1.5-5 lakh; premium INR5-25 lakh. Mix by ticket size: 60-70% lower ticket, 20-25% medium, 10-12% higher ticket.
Product mix by share of sales: rings about 28%, studded mangalsutra 25-27%, earrings 15-17%, necklaces about 10%, bangles 5-6% each. Platinum is a very small share.

Jewellery cost composition now about 50-55% gold, 30-35% diamond, 15-20% making (earlier 15-20% gold and 60-65% diamond). Management says gross margin % may fall as gold share rises but rupee margin should hold or grow.

Brand spend 3-4% of top-line annually; brand value not yet loaded into diamond pricing, so gross margin could improve as brand builds. Competitive set cited: Gargi Fashion Jewellery (14k gold, H/I colour diamonds) as a differentiated sister brand.
risks_watch: Gold-price sensitivity: SSG guidance is conditional on stable gold; management said a sharp rally drove the ~40% FY26 SSG, and a rally would lower gross margin %.
Inventory turn dilution from 6-7 new EBOs in FY27 at about 0.75x turn and slow early-stage ramp; EBO breakeven 8-12 months in Maharashtra and 18-24 months outside.
Execution across 15 stores in 24 months, including 2 out-of-state stores in FY27 and a North India / mall push outside Maharashtra.
Related-party and governance questions: sister company Gargi Fashion Jewellery sells similar product at 14k gold; management shared bandwidth across two entities, and Gargi lacks a CEO.
Lab-grown diamond competition and changes in import duty or GST; management says price effects are statutory and uniform across brands.
Buyer count and disaggregated customer data were not disclosed; management offered to share by email, so customer-growth metrics remain open.
key_quotes: Our inventory turn are at 1.31 times in FY26 as our store network continues to mature.
SSG, I am expecting around 25% to 30%, it will not be less than 25% to 30%.

So in value term that it is there, but if gold prices remain stable, I am expecting 25% to 30%, but if gold prices shoot up just like last year, it again can match with the previous year's SSG growth.
So I don't primarily expect any dilution of the equity, but after getting settled by 2030, I will be expanding out of the borrowings in future.
summary.management_tone: "Confident and expansive on growth, brand and capital model, but evasive on forward rupee numbers (declined precise revenue projections) and on buyer count and customer acquisition cost. Management was firm that gold-price moves do not hit demand and that the EBITDA margin dip reflects standalone costs."

adds.what: 14 remaining EBO/COCO stores of 15 planned over 24 months (6-7 in FY27, balance FY28); one already open
EBO stores at INR20-25 crore capex per outlet
2 out-of-state stores planned in FY27 within the 15-store programme

growth.why: Management guides 25-30% top-line growth and SSG of at least 25% for FY27-28, backed by 14 remaining stores (6-7 in FY27), a 2-store out-of-state plan and a 40% SSG base in FY26, with INR287 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for expansion; the store specifics are concrete but no firm order or contract numbers were given for the SSG guide itself.
